scope: CBSE Class 6 Science · Curiosity · Chapter 11 · Nature’s Treasures
claimBoundary: Deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios only. This is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, drinking-water or potability certification, environmental-impact certification, field-safety certification, conservation permit, school-specific pacing proof or permission to enter hazardous sites, collect contaminated materials, handle fuels, inspect traffic, view the Sun directly, climb roofs or consume untreated water.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 11 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked reasoning or mastery assessment, a privacy-safe learner action and an observable mastery criterion while preserving freshwater/potability, resource-timescale, renewable-impact and field/fuel/sun/electrical safety boundaries.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes that because Earth contains a great deal of water, usable freshwater must be abundant everywhere and conservation is unnecessary.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Interpret supplied water-distribution diagrams or data to distinguish total water, saline water and accessible freshwater, then propose household or school conservation actions without collecting or drinking samples.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains why total water abundance does not guarantee accessible freshwater and identifies at least two defensible conservation actions.

scenarios.need: Learner treats clear-looking water as automatically safe to drink and uses appearance alone as proof of potability.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare supplied descriptions of clear, cloudy and treated water and reject appearance-only potability claims; no tasting, drinking or home testing is required.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: States that visual clarity alone cannot establish drinking-water safety and distinguishes observation from verified potability evidence.

scenarios.need: Learner proposes breath-holding, direct Sun viewing, roof climbing or touching solar/electrical equipment as proof activities for air or solar-energy concepts.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Reject the unsafe activity and use supplied air-composition models, food-chain diagrams, solar photographs or electricity-generation datasets instead.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains the intended air or solar-energy concept using supplied evidence while explicitly rejecting breath-holding, direct-Sun, rooftop and electrical-access hazards.

scenarios.need: Learner says soil is only crushed rock or treats rocks and minerals as interchangeable categories, then proposes tasting or handling unknown material to identify it.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use supplied component diagrams and labelled clean sample cards to compare soil, rocks and minerals without tasting, licking, scraping or handling unknown materials.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Describes soil as a multi-component system, distinguishes rocks from minerals and selects a non-ingestion, non-destructive evidence method.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes that visiting roadsides, rubbish areas, active quarries or mines is necessary to obtain authentic evidence about soil, rocks, minerals or extraction.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Reject hazardous field collection and use supplied photographs, maps, museum/public-science resources or clean adult-approved classroom samples instead.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Identifies contamination, traffic, unstable ground, machinery or restricted-access hazards and reconstructs the resource evidence from safe supplied sources.

scenarios.need: Learner classifies coal or petroleum as renewable simply because they are natural, ignoring the difference between geological formation time and human consumption time.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Sort supplied resource cards by replenishment timescale and compare geological formation with human-use timescales without handling any fuel.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly classifies fossil fuels as non-renewable on human timescales and justifies the classification using replenishment rate rather than the label ‘natural’.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes renewable energy means unlimited supply with zero environmental impact and therefore ignores materials, land, infrastructure or siting constraints.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare supplied lifecycle-style evidence for sunlight, wind and fossil-fuel options, separating replenishment of the energy resource from impacts of the technology that captures or uses it.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains that renewable describes replenishment, not zero impact, and identifies at least one realistic technology or siting constraint.

scenarios.need: Learner needs offline resource-conservation practice without uploading location, photographing utilities, visiting filling stations, standing near traffic, handling fuels or exposing household consumption details.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Complete cached text, diagrams and supplied synthetic energy/resource datasets locally; no sensors, uploads, precise location, household bills, fuel handling, roadside surveys or filling-station visits are required.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes the offline synthetic task using supplied evidence only, classifies resources by timescale, states impact limits and avoids personal-data or hazardous field disclosure.
